title: Bind conservation and entropy to the exact finite-mass equation
statement: For d_ij=grad log f_i/m_i-grad log f_j/m_j and F_ij=f_i(v)f_j(w), weak moment differentiation is -1/2 sum c_ij int F_ij a d_ij dot(grad phi_i/m_i-grad phi_j/m_j). This preserves EACH n_i, total momentum P=sum m_i int v f_i and kinetic energy E=1/2 sum m_i int |v|^2 f_i. Entropy production D_H=1/2 sum c_ij int F_ij |v-w|^-1 |P_(v-w)d_ij|^2=1/2 sum c_ij mu_ij^-2 J_ij, mu_ij=m_i m_j/(m_i+m_j). With rho=sum m_i n_i,u=P/rho,Theta=(2E-|P|^2/rho)/[3(n1+n2)], Maxwellians have actual n_i and mass-dependent variance Theta/m_i; relative entropy plus integral D_H equals its initial value on the classical interval. This is an integral dissipation budget, not a supremum or derivative bound for Fisher or J_ij; both species evolve at finite recoil.
